results.request: Year 3 science. Teach the class about dinosaurs.

teacherIntent.subject: Science
teacherIntent.learningGoal: Pupils understand that fossils show what dinosaurs were like.
teacherIntent.requiredEvidence: A pupil says what a fossil can show about a dinosaur, including what it ate.

claims.text: Dinosaurs were animals that lived a very long time ago.
A fossil is a trace of a living thing kept in rock.
Sharp fossil teeth cut meat, so that the fossil shows a meat-eating dinosaur.
A dinosaur egg is a round fossil with a shell.
The shell kept the baby inside, because a thin shell would have broken.
Some dinosaur bones are hollow.
Hollow bones made the body lighter, so that a large dinosaur could still move.
Fossils, tooth shape and the rock layer together show how a dinosaur lived.
Some dinosaurs could breathe fire when they were angry.

results.request: Year 4 science. Teach how sharks' adaptations help them live and hunt in the sea.

teacherIntent.subject: Science
teacherIntent.learningGoal: Pupils explain how a shark's body helps it live and hunt in the sea.
teacherIntent.requiredEvidence: A pupil explains how gills, the tail, or the body shape helps a shark in the water.

claims.text: A shark is a fish with fins, gills and a tail.
A shark has gills on the side of its head.
Gills take oxygen from the water so that a shark can breathe.
A shark has a strong tail.
The tail pushes water backwards so that the shark moves forward.
A shark has a pointed body shape.
The pointed shape lets water slide past the body so that the shark slows down less.
Fins, tail and gills work together as one system that lets a shark hunt in open water.
Sharks keep fish numbers in balance, so the ocean stays healthy.

results.request: Year 5 history. Teach how Henry VIII's break with Rome changed England.

teacherIntent.subject: History
teacherIntent.learningGoal: Pupils explain how Henry VIII's break with Rome changed the church in England.
teacherIntent.requiredEvidence: A pupil names the break with Rome and one change that followed for the church in England.

claims.text: Henry VIII was king of England from 1509 to 1547.
In 1534 the Act of Supremacy said Henry, not the Pope, was head of the Church in England.
Henry wanted a male heir, so he asked Rome to end his marriage to Catherine of Aragon.
When Rome refused, Henry's break with Rome let him control the English church.
Catherine of Aragon was Henry's first wife.
A monastery was a religious house that owned land.
The break closed many monasteries, so that their land and wealth went to the crown and new owners.
Historians still disagree about whether Henry cared more about religion or about power.
claims.uncertainty: Motive is interpreted, not a single settled fact.

claims.text: Henry said the exact words 'I am the only church' in 1534.

results.request: Year 4 science. Explain why sharks are mammals.

teacherIntent.subject: Science
teacherIntent.learningGoal: Pupils explain why sharks are mammals.
teacherIntent.requiredEvidence: A pupil gives the reason sharks are mammals.

claims.text: Sharks are mammals.
Sharks are fish, not mammals.
Gills take oxygen from the water so that a shark can breathe.
Mammals feed milk to their young and breathe air with lungs.
A shark does not feed its young on milk, because a shark is a fish.
Sharks have scales rather than hair, so that they are not classed as mammals.
Whales and dolphins are mammals, because they breathe air and feed milk.
A shark's skin is covered in tiny scales called denticles.
Denticles let water flow smoothly over the skin, so that the shark wastes less effort.
Lungs and gills are different systems for getting oxygen.
